header: Date: 2026-01-21 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (CTO - Aurelius), Elena Soto (ML Eng Lead - Aurelius), Tom Weaver (SRE - Aurelius)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review lab benchmark results comparing Redwood inference runtime vs incumbent provider across latency and throughput. Covered p50/p95 numbers, batching and KV cache tuning, routing fallbacks, and next steps for extended load tests and pricing for dedicated slots.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching effects
Dedicated capacity request and cost model
transcript:
[00:00:00] Marcus Lee: Hi everyone, Marcus from Redwood. Thanks for joining, we know it's a hectic week. quick sound check?
[00:00:10] Rajiv Patel: Hi Marcus, sounds fine. Elena and Tom here too.
[00:00:18] Elena Soto: Yep, good here. audio's a bit fuzzy at times but okay.
[00:00:25] Priya Nair: Great. We'll jump in — we have the updated bench spreadsheet and the raw logs link in the follow-up, Marcus will share.
[00:00:35] Marcus Lee: Cool. Agenda — review the numbers we ran overnight, discuss tuning changes (KV cache, batching window), compare to your incumbent provider, and agree next steps.
[00:00:47] Tom Weaver: Sounds good. main thing for us is p95 under sustained 70% traffic and how that scales to 90%.
[00:00:55] Marcus Lee: Totally. quick primer: test rig was 8-simultaneous-clients ramping to 500 concurrent connections, 512-token gen, single model variant "rwd-13b-instr" (we said that in the notes but transcript might say r w d). we ran both on your baseline infra and on Redwood hosted lane with identical instance types (A100 equiv).
[00:01:18] Elena Soto: Right, we wanted apples-to-apples.
[00:01:22] Priya Nair: Notes — we enabled prefix KV caching for repeated prompts in the Redwood run; that shaved tokens/time for warm sessions. also enabled dynamic batch window at 30ms.
[00:01:38] Rajiv Patel: OK show us numbers.
[00:01:41] Marcus Lee: Slide 3 in the sheet — p50/p95 latency (ms) for 512-token, 70% load: Redwood p50=88ms, p95=175ms; Incumbent p50=210ms, p95=430ms. throughput per GPU: Redwood 320 requests/min, Incumbent 180 requests/min.
[00:02:05] Elena Soto: Whoa that's a big spread on p95. Is that with KV cache warm across clients or cold start included?
[00:02:12] Priya Nair: Good question — these numbers are mixed. We kept 60% of sessions warm (prefix reuse) to reflect your traffic pattern; cold starts are in separate tab. Cold start p95 for Redwood rose to ~420ms but that's for the first few tokens while KV warms.
[00:02:29] Tom Weaver: Incumbent cold starts were worse for us, like 800-900ms.
[00:02:34] Marcus Lee: Right. also note batching effects — Redwood dynamic batching increased packing efficiency by ~1.8x which explains higher requests/min.
[00:02:45] Rajiv Patel: Are these numbers from the dedicated slot or hosted?
[00:02:49] Priya Nair: Hosted lane but using dedicated-like instance sizes. We can run on Redwood Dedicated pool too — you requested a dedicated slot trial.
[00:02:57] Elena Soto: We did. need to know cost delta vs incumbent if we reserve.
[00:03:02] Marcus Lee: We'll include a cost model in the updated spreadsheet. rough delta based on this throughput: Redwood per-token compute is lower because of batching and cache, so unit cost comes down ~25-35% in our estimates. We'll put detailed numbers.
[00:03:17] Elena Soto: Good. What about model quantization? we saw some quality drop with 4-bit in other runs.
[00:03:24] Priya Nair: We tried 4-bit QAT on a small sample — latency improved another 15-20% but we flagged one edge case in hallucination tests. It's in the evaluation tab. You can choose hybrid: quantize non-critical layers and keep others full precision.
[00:03:39] Rajiv Patel: Hmm, quality tradeoff is a blocker for prod.
[00:03:43] Marcus Lee: Understood. that's why Redwood Optimize suggests per-workload quant profiles — we'll recommend candidate profiles for your prompt set.
[00:03:51] Tom Weaver: Back to p95 — that 175ms seems optimistic. can you walk through percentiles across time? like p90/p95/p99?
[00:03:59] Priya Nair: Sure. p90=132ms, p95=175ms, p99=410ms for 70% load. under 90% load p95 rises to 265ms, and p99 to ~620ms. Incumbent at 90% had p95 520ms.
[00:04:18] Elena Soto: Did you instrument queue times vs GPU inference time? we want to isolate scheduling overhead.
[00:04:24] Marcus Lee: Yes, we captured breakdown: average scheduling/queue wait at 70% was 22ms on Redwood, GPU inference 60ms, post-processing 6ms. Incumbent scheduling was larger, ~130ms, inference 70ms — so scheduling and batching inefficiencies are a big part of their higher p95.
[00:04:43] Rajiv Patel: That aligns with what we've seen.
[00:04:46] Tom Weaver: Any noisy neighbor effects in the shared runs?
[00:04:49] Priya Nair: We ran both on isolated instances to avoid noisy neighbors; for the hosted config we used isolated vCPU/GPU allocations.
[00:04:57] Marcus Lee: Quick aside — there were a few transcribe glitches in the logs about KV spelled K-V. ignore that.
[00:05:03] Elena Soto: Ha. noted.
[00:05:06] Marcus Lee: Next I want to call out a weird outlier series between 00:22 and 00:26 in the raw logs — we saw a spike on Incumbent where p99 shot up to 1.2s when the cluster OOM'd on a retry storm. we caught the trace id in the sheet.
[00:05:20] Rajiv Patel: Did you simulate retries? our client library has a 3x backoff we didn't want to trigger.
[00:05:25] Priya Nair: We used your prod-like client settings, 2 retries with jitter. the incumbent cluster reacted poorly to bursts — queuing cascaded. Redwood's routing fallback kept requests to warmed nodes and avoided the retry storm.
[00:05:38] Tom Weaver: Good! show me the routing policy in practice.
[00:05:41] Marcus Lee: Slide 7 summarises policy: route by latency-first to warmed nodes, fallback to lower-capacity but cheaper pools if latency SLO breached. we can set hard SLOs per endpoint.
[00:05:54] Elena Soto: So if we set SLO 300ms, it will route to dedicated capacity when predicted breach occurs?
[00:06:00] Priya Nair: Yes — predictive routing uses short-term windows to choose verticals. it's in beta but used in this test.
[00:06:06] Rajiv Patel: We need audit logs for routing decisions for SEC/reg compliance.
[00:06:11] Marcus Lee: Redwood Console provides per-request tracing and an audit log export. we'll attach the export sample.
[00:06:18] Elena Soto: Please do. Also SSO and SAML for RBAC — who owns that?
[00:06:22] Marcus Lee: Security team handles SSO integrations. I'll loop in our security PM in the follow-up.
[00:06:28] Tom Weaver: Cool.
[00:06:31] Marcus Lee: Back to tuning — Priya, tell them about the KV policy change we tried overnight.
[00:06:35] Priya Nair: We reduced hot-prefix eviction to 4k entries instead of default 8k which lowered cache churn for your workload and improved p95 by about 18ms in warm sessions. also increased max batch size to 32 which improved GPU utilization without impacting p99 in our runs.
[00:06:52] Elena Soto: how about tail latency when bumping batch size? sometimes p99 suffers.
[00:06:56] Priya Nair: Right. We saw negligible p99 effect up to batch 32 because dynamic batching avoids holding requests for long — window remains 30ms. beyond 50 batch size we saw p99 deterioration.
[00:07:08] Rajiv Patel: Any parameter we should change client-side?
[00:07:10] Priya Nair: You can loosen client-side per-request timeout slightly to let batching collect, but set a global 2.5s timeout to catch runaway requests. also prioritize short responses with fast paths.
[00:07:20] Tom Weaver: On the cost side, will batching force bigger memory footprint?
[00:07:24] Marcus Lee: Some, but it's amortized by better throughput; memory went up ~6% in the run. okay want to open it up for questions?
[00:07:32] Elena Soto: Yes — why did Redwood cold-start p95 hit 420ms? we expected lower.
[00:07:37] Priya Nair: Cold-start includes container spin-up plus KV warm; if you pre-warm with a small keep-alive or use reserved dedicated slots cold starts go away. for hosted we can enable a warm pool.
[00:07:49] Rajiv Patel: Pre-warm cost?
[00:07:51] Marcus Lee: We'll add pre-warm pricing to the cost model. it's typically a small hourly fee relative to reserved GPU.
[00:07:59] Tom Weaver: On data retention — logs show request-level traces, are these PII-stripped?
[00:08:04] Marcus Lee: Default log capture redacts obvious PII, and we have encryption-at-rest with KMS. for SOC2 we can show retention policies and masking.
[00:08:13] Elena Soto: Great.
[00:08:16] Priya Nair: Quick demo note — we also tried a quantized run at 4-bit during the evening tests; saw latency down 18% but one eval prompt in the hallucination suite failed threshold. we flagged that prompt in the eval tab with the example.
[00:08:31] Rajiv Patel: We'll review that prompt. if it's uncommon maybe acceptable.
[00:08:35] Marcus Lee: Agreed. We'll recommend candidate quant profiles per your prompts.
[00:08:39] Tom Weaver: Anything on model switching / fallback? we may want a cheaper model for non-critical responses.
[00:08:45] Priya Nair: Yes — routing supports model-variant fallback. set rules by endpoint to call smaller quantized model for low-cost paths and larger for high-criticality requests. the system can transparently swap and keep session KV where compatible.
[00:08:59] Elena Soto: Nice. how do we validate quality regressions after swapping?
[00:09:02] Marcus Lee: Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets and sends alerts if output quality drops relative to baseline. we'll set up a focused evaluation harness for your top 200 prompts.
[00:09:13] Rajiv Patel: Sounds good.
[00:09:16] Marcus Lee: Time check — we're at 9 minutes in the call log here, but full session had more meat; I'll highlight the log sections we'll attach.
[00:09:25] Priya Nair: One more item from the lab — we tried an A/B route with FastServe (competitor) as a low-cost fallback; their p95 was between Redwood and Incumbent but had higher variance. we'd recommend against them for critical flows.
[00:09:40] Elena Soto: ok noted.
[00:09:43] Tom Weaver: Regarding SLOs, can you show the per-route SLO dashboards in Console?
[00:09:48] Marcus Lee: We'll record a short screen share and include screenshots.
[00:09:52] Rajiv Patel: Next steps recap?
[00:09:54] Marcus Lee: Sure — Marcus to share updated spreadsheet and raw logs; Priya to send tuning notes; Elena to run extended load test; Rajiv to confirm security contacts. We'll also tentatively schedule a dedicated-pricing deep dive Jan 29.
[00:10:10] Elena Soto: That matches our notes. anything else?
[00:10:13] Tom Weaver: One ask — can Redwood run the next test with the client-side retry set to 1 instead of 2 to see impact?
[00:10:18] Marcus Lee: Yes we can. we'll run a quick run tomorrow morning and share delta.
[00:10:23] Rajiv Patel: Great. thanks team.
[00:10:26] Marcus Lee: Thanks all. we'll send notes and links. bye.
[00:10:30] --- END OF MEETING SUMMARY SNIPPET ---
[00:22:00] NOTE: The raw log contained a 4-minute window where incumbent cluster OOMed (trace ids included in sheet), causing p99 spikes to 1.2s.
[00:34:15] NOTE: Priya's tuning (eviction 4k, batch max 32) measured p95 improvement of ~18ms for warm sessions in the separate tuning run.
[00:40:12] NOTE: Cold-start test (no warm pool) p95 Redwood ~420ms; with pre-warm reserved slots p95 < 190ms in our sim.
[00:45:30] ACTION: Marcus to upload revised spreadsheet and raw logs to shared drive; Priya to upload SE tuning notes and a short demo video of routing console."
